summary.headline: Regional School Committee approves a 2027 trip to Spain and reconsiders to renew its food service management contract.
summary.summary: The Regional School Committee elected its leadership for the upcoming year and welcomed new members before approving an international student field trip to Spain for April 2027. Following discussion on cafeteria staff morale and food quality, the committee initially voted down a one-year renewal with Whitsons Culinary Group before reconsidering and approving the contract. The committee also adopted revisions to the 2026-2027 student handbook and accepted financial updates, including over $411,000 in state special education circuit breaker relief.

topics.title: Welcome of new members and election of officers
topics.summary: The committee welcomed new members Denise Eddy, Megan Sanko, and Erin Treglia. In accordance with committee rotation policy between Northborough and Southborough, the committee elected Northborough representative Joan Frank as chair, Chris Lacasse as vice chair, and Kathleen Harragan as secretary.
key_details: New members seated: Denise Eddy, Megan Sanko, and Erin Treglia
Joan Frank elected chair
Chris Lacasse elected vice chair
Kathleen Harragan elected secretary

topics.title: Algonquin Robotics Team presentation and demonstration
topics.summary: Team 1100, the Algonquin Robotics Team, gave an overview of their season, team growth, community outreach, and robot design process. Students demonstrated the robot picking up and launching foam balls using computer vision and AprilTags for automated target acquisition.
key_details: Team grew from approximately 20 students to nearly 60 members over three years
Qualified for the New England District Championship and Massachusetts State Championship
Won the Judges Award at WPI and Sustainability Award at Western New England University
Hosted a First Lego League qualifier with over 50 teams at Algonquin

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the open meeting minutes from April 15, 2026, accepted private donations totaling over $9,400 for sports facility scoreboards and school events, and voted to enter executive session to discuss collective bargaining strategy.
key_details: Minutes of April 15, 2026 approved unanimously
Accepted $9,000 in donated materials and labor from Gamache Construction to restore varsity baseball and softball scoreboards
Accepted $200 from parent April Cimorelli via MassMutual match and $200 from Wegmans for the Culture Festival
Voted to enter executive session regarding Unit C collective bargaining negotiations
topics.outcome: Minutes, donations, and executive session motion approved

topics.title: International field trip to Spain (April 2027)
topics.summary: Spanish teacher Evan Greenwald presented a proposal for an eight-day educational tour to Spain scheduled for April 17 to April 24, 2027, organized through EF Educational Tours. The trip is open to all Algonquin students and will cover UNESCO World Heritage sites and cultural landmarks across Madrid, Segovia, Salamanca, Merida, and Toledo.
key_details: Dates: April 17 to April 24, 2027, during April school vacation
Estimated early enrollment cost is $3,989 per student
Chaperone-to-student ratio is 1:6 per EF Tours policy
Open to all students regardless of Spanish language enrollment
Includes group fundraising options and EF scholarship opportunities
topics.why_it_matters: Approves an out-of-country travel opportunity for high school students costing roughly $4,000 per participant.

topics.title: Applied Arts and Technology Department update
topics.summary: Department Head George Clark presented a review of applied arts, business, computer science, family and consumer sciences, and technology engineering courses. Clark announced his retirement after 30 years in the district, introducing Christine Norman as the incoming department head.
key_details: Retirement of Department Head George Clark after 30 years
Incoming department head announced as Christine Norman
New course offerings for 2026-2027: AP Business and Personal Finance, Working with Young Children, and Evolution of Style Through Fashion Technology
Student-run business 'Daily Grind' generated over $6,000 in revenue over three years

topics.title: Student handbook updates for 2026-2027
topics.summary: Assistant Principal Andy McGowan presented updates to the 2026-2027 student handbook. Additions clarify rules regarding outside coursework credit, criteria for course waivers, bus behavioral expectations, security cameras on school grounds, and legal requirements concerning parental curriculum requests.
key_details: Outside coursework completed through private programs will not be accepted for graduation credit except under pre-approved limited circumstances
Course waivers may be granted in exceptional circumstances by school administration in consultation with counselors
Added policy language regarding audio/video recording on buses and security cameras
Incorporated statutory language regarding parental requests for curriculum accommodation

topics.title: Whitsons Food Service contract renewal
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the first-year performance of Whitsons Culinary Group and considered a contract renewal for the 2026-2027 school year with a 3.9 percent fee increase tied to the Consumer Price Index. After members expressed concerns about food quality, student satisfaction, and staff morale, an initial motion to renew failed 3-4-2, but the committee reconsidered and voted 8-1 to approve the one-year renewal after learning that failing to renew would leave the district without food service vendor options for the fall.
key_details: Whitsons contract renewal includes a 3.9 percent increase tied to CPI
Administrative fee increases from 5.0 cents to 5.2 cents per meal; management fee from 11.6 cents to 12.1 cents per meal
Food service program operated at a net loss of $60,801 through the first three quarters, driven by kitchen equipment repairs and staff training
Whitsons contract contains a guaranteed minimum return of $29,491, meaning Whitsons must cover shortfalls up to that guaranteed profit level
Initial vote to renew failed 3-4 with 2 abstentions; reconsidered and approved 8-1
topics.why_it_matters: Authorizes the management and fees for school breakfast and lunch programs across the district for the upcoming academic year.

topics.title: Subcommittee and liaison appointments
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and assigned members to various subcommittees and municipal liaison posts for the 2026-2027 school year.
key_details: Denise Eddy and Megan Sanko joined the collective bargaining subcommittee
Joan Frank volunteered to sign payroll and accounts payable warrants with Jen Ryan
Joan Frank will serve as select board liaison
topics.outcome: Assignments designated; members will submit additional preferences to administration

topics.title: Principal and superintendent reports
topics.summary: Student representative Madison Wilson and Principal Sean Bevan reviewed end-of-year events, upcoming graduation on June 6, and senior class milestones. Bevan noted ongoing district preparations for pending state legislation restricting student cell phone use, and introduced a new freshman 'Math Lab' course to provide extra support for students struggling in Algebra I.
key_details: School is preparing for statewide cell phone restriction legislation expected for next school year
Full 1:1 Chromebook program will be in place for all four high school grades in fall 2026
New single-semester 'Math Lab' course launching in 2026-2027 for approximately 30 to 35 freshmen needing remedial math support
Graduation scheduled for Saturday, June 6, on the football field
Student Katie Campbell will represent Massachusetts at the Special Olympics USA Games in Minnesota

topics.title: District financial reports and circuit breaker relief
topics.summary: Director of Finance and Operations Rebecca Perehudoff reported on the budget as of April 30, 2026, showing an unencumbered operating budget balance of $484,507 (1.63 percent of the operational budget). The district received $394,642 in state special education circuit breaker extraordinary relief, with an additional $17,027 recently confirmed by the state Department of Elementary and Secondary Education.
key_details: Operational budget balance stands at $484,507 or 1.63 percent remaining
State awarded $411,669 in total circuit breaker extraordinary relief due to high special education costs exceeding prior-year thresholds by over 25 percent
General fund and revenue statements approved through April 30, 2026
Final fiscal year local assessment payments due June 1
topics.outcome: Monthly general fund and revenue statements approved unanimously
topics.why_it_matters: Confirms the regional district's positive year-end budget balance and over $411,000 in unexpected state special education reimbursements.

public_comment.summary: An Algonquin cafeteria employee of Whitney Street expressed concerns on behalf of cafeteria staff regarding Whitsons Food Service. She noted staff morale is low, the cafeteria ran out of meals or experienced shortages, pre-shaped frozen cookies containing numerous preservatives replaced fresh homemade cookies, and employees feel their concerns are not being heard.

Comprehensive review and progress report on Whitsons Food Service contract
